ownership_reason: ZipUtil.toDosTime packs the DOS time word as (year-1980)<<25 | month<<21 | day<<16 | hour<<11 | minute<<5 | getSeconds()>>1: the minute field starts at bit 5, so the seconds field has only 5 bits (0-31) and must hold seconds/2 (DOS two-second resolution; odd seconds are dropped by design). The existing, passing ZipUtilTest.testZipLong rebuilds the same word independently with cal.get(Calendar.SECOND) >> 1, which pins the encoder's halving. The inverse, ZipUtil.dosToJavaTime (used by ZipFile.populateFromCentralDirectory for every entry, and by ZipUtil.fromDosTime), must therefore multiply the 5-bit field by 2; it sets Calendar.SECOND from the raw field (dosTime & 0x1f) without the doubling, so an even second s is read back as s/2 (46 -> 23). The writer (ZipArchiveOutputStream.writeCentralFileHeader) and reader (ZipFile.populateFromCentralDirectory, ZipLong.getValue) only move the 4-byte word unchanged. Dropping the halving in toDosTime instead overflows seconds >= 32 into the minute field (the trigger then reads 10:21:14) and breaks testZipLong; restoring the doubling in dosToJavaTime alone makes the trigger and the full suite pass.

compensating.why: one-line encoder edit: toDosTime stores the full second count instead of seconds/2
one-line reader edit: populateFromCentralDirectory decodes the central-directory time word through ZipUtil.fromDosTime
one-line encoder edit: toDosTime rounds the halved seconds up instead of truncating
